newsitem.title: UKRAINE: AGROKHLEB-Ukraine works to liberalise agro market.
newsitem.headline: AGROKHLEB-Ukraine works to liberalise agro market.

text.p: The following is a direct contribution from SovEcon Ltd, an independent research organisation specialising in agricultural production and trade in the former Soviet Union, in association with Ukragroconsult, a private Ukrainian agricultural consultancy based in Kiev.
UKRAINE WORKS TO LIBERALISE GRAIN MARKET
KIEV, June 2 - The Ukrainian government approved in May a resolution entitled "On the Regulations of Distribution of Grain Grown In 1997".
According to the document, the government is authorised to purchase about five million tonnes of domestic grain for which it has contracted.
Similarly, regional administrations are authorised to purchase about three million tonnes of grain already contracted for.
Ukraine's remaining grain shall be at the full and complete disposal of producers and companies which buy under barter contracts.
If the government fails to pay for its contracted grain before January 1, 1998, farmers are free to market the unpaid grain as they wish.
One of the aims of the document is to avoid last year's local prohibitions which resulted in grain being locked up and exports prevented.
The resolution prohibits central and local authorities from interfering in the grain market, including in exports.

It also stipulates that the volume of state procurements will be reduced in 1998 and envisages the demonopolisation and privatisation of Khlib of Ukraine -- the state grain-buying agency -- and the privatisation of silos.
